clue.text: City scent surrounds northern inlet

parts.note: Bristol is a city in south-west England

indicators.note: the perfume's name goes round the abbreviation, so it is the outer piece here

parts.note: Chanel is a famous brand of perfume

explanation.surface: Someone notices a city's perfume drifting around a small northern bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounds' puts N inside CHANEL to make CHANNEL. The inlet is the wide sea arm between south Wales and south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea arm is a broad estuary-like stretch of water reaching inland, a large inlet of the Atlantic.

clue.text: Knock around trouble and special officer appears

indicators.note: the word for a knock is wrapped around the word for trouble

parts.note: a biff is a blow or knock
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A scuffle breaks out and a special constable turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the container: the blow word is split open after its first letter to take in the trouble word.
explanation.definitionFit: A court enforcement agent who seizes goods or serves writs is a sheriff's officer with particular duties.

clue.text: Dine out with company? Odd. Poor behaviour

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of dine are rearranged

parts.note: rum is an old-fashioned word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Someone eats out with company, and the evening's conduct turns peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal for 'Dine'; the question mark after 'Odd' hides that it is old slang supplying the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is a lack of propriety, conduct that breaks good manners.

clue.text: Experience bite

definitions.meaning: to ... freedom is to experience it briefly
a bite of food is a small ... of it

explanation.definitionFit: To sample something is both to undergo it briefly and to take a small mouthful.

clue.text: Successful one's to produce nil traces?

definitions.text: Successful one's to produce nil traces?

indicators.note: the letters of the words that follow are worked into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A good thief makes sure nothing is left behind as evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to produce' rearranges NIL TRACES. Read as a whole, the clue says a skilled thief leaves no clues behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who commits theft is one; a successful one leaves no evidence.

clue.text: See 1
Surface with bit of chemical corrosion

indicators.note: a bit of the word means just its first letter here

parts.note: rust is the corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: A metal surface shows a patch of chemical attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' takes C, the first letter of 'chemical'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard outer layer, as on bread or the earth, is its surface.

clue.text: Sailor gave commands, but with no time, resigned

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor

indicators.note: the time abbreviation is taken away from the word for giving orders

parts.note: to dictate is to give orders

explanation.surface: A naval officer who issued orders steps down at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes one T from DICTATED, leaving DICATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up a throne or office formally is to step down from it.

clue.text: Midday over the east. Not a person in sight

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting over another comes before it

parts.note: noon is midday
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: At noon the eastern horizon is deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobody at all; an empty scene has nobody visible.

clue.text: Learn after training about books. That'll shed some light

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation for books
training reshapes the word learn, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A student revises after lessons, then sheds light on the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after training' signals the anagram of 'Learn' (giving LAERN), and 'about' wraps those letters round the books abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp in a case, carried or hung, gives out illumination.

clue.text: No attempt to work in Asian river

indicators.note: no attempt means the word for attempt is dropped from what follows

parts.note: industry is hard work, diligence
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Nobody bothers to try working near an Asian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes TRY from INDUSTRY. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The great waterway flowing through Pakistan to the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Bypass the soft stuff and lower to convenient figure

parts.note: to round an obstacle is to go around it, to bypass it
down is the soft fine feathers of a bird

explanation.surface: Someone skirts round the feather pillows and lowers the price.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce a number to the nearest whole or tidy value below it.

clue.text: Stormy client gets upset about people

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the word for people
the word client is upset, knocked over into a new letter order

parts.note: men is a plain word for people

explanation.surface: A customer loses their temper with some staff in foul weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets upset' signals the anagram of 'client' (giving INCLET), and 'about' wraps it round the people word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclement weather is harsh and rough, cold or wet.

clue.text: Salesman in church fabric

indicators.note: one word sits in another, so the salesman goes inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a rep, short for representative, is a travelling salesman

explanation.surface: A salesman visits a church to sell some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin crinkled cloth, often silk, is a type of fabric.

clue.text: Public meeting in debate "Of turning to drink"

indicators.note: turning means the little word of is read backwards

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: At a public debate someone speaks on the slide into drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses OF to FO; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembly where matters are openly discussed, like the Roman public square.

clue.text: Some acts of extravagant emotion

parts.note: read as a stage show in several acts, a play full of overblown feeling, or as such feeling in life

explanation.definitionFit: A sensational play with exaggerated characters, or behaviour full of overblown feeling.

clue.text: Wager little in pub (neither here nor there)

indicators.note: the wager and the small word go inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a bet is a wager
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A small bet is placed in a pub, of uncertain merit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals a container: the wager and Scots 'little' go inside the pub word. The bracketed words are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Intermediate, in the middle position, belonging to neither side.

clue.text: Projections from the top set

parts.note: the top set reads as the upper row of a mouth, and the projections as protruding ones

explanation.definitionFit: Upper front incisors that stick out forward, from the upper jaw.

clue.text: Evade tax? Clause, initially misconstrued, unearthed

indicators.note: misconstrued means wrongly put together, so the letters are rearranged
initially takes just the first letter of clause

explanation.surface: A tax dodge comes to light after a contract term is misread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives C from 'Clause'; 'misconstrued' rearranges EVADETAX with C.
explanation.definitionFit: Dug out, brought up from the ground.

clue.text: I'm cloth, ie prepared for sermonising

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, worked up from the letters into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A vicar announces their vestments are ready for preaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges IMCLOTHIE. 'the cloth' is the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to homilies, the art of preaching moral talks.

clue.text: From which I'll topple — if pushed?

definitions.text: From which I'll topple — if pushed?

indicators.note: From says the letters come out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A climber stands on a summit, afraid of being shoved off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' takes letters straight from 'whicH I'LL TOPple'. Read whole, the clue describes the high place one could be pushed off.
explanation.definitionFit: The summit of a rise, from which a shove would send one tumbling.

clue.text: Cuts keys, we hear

definitions.meaning: to dock is to cut short, as a tail or wages
keys sounds like quays, and quays are wharves for ships

explanation.surface: A locksmith cuts some keys, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Docking is cutting short; quays are harbour landing places.

clue.text: Sentimental about heartless teacher awkward to deal with

indicators.note: the sentimental word goes about, around, the trimmed teacher

parts.note: soppy is sentimental, mushy

indicators.note: heartless means the inside of teacher is gone, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A soppy schoolteacher who has lost all compassion becomes hard to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' keeps only the first and last letters of 'teacher'; 'about' puts the sentimental word around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad-tempered and uncooperative, the sort who is difficult.

clue.text: Copper back in hat, shining

indicators.note: the turned symbol goes in the word for hat

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

indicators.note: back means the chemical symbol is read backwards

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman's helmet gleams as he walks back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the copper symbol and 'in' puts it inside the hat word. 'Copper' suggests a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear and bright, as in lucid, luminous light.

clue.text: Kind of section to study integrated circuit

parts.note: to con is to study or learn carefully

explanation.surface: A student is told to look into a microchip.
explanation.definitionFit: A conic section is a curve made by slicing a cone.

clue.text: A fetching dog, exceptional trier always

indicators.note: exceptional suggests out of the ordinary, so the letters of trier are rearranged

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: An attractive dog that always tries exceptionally hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptional' turns TRIER into RETRI. 'fetching' looks like 'attractive' but means a dog bred to fetch game.
explanation.definitionFit: A gundog breed trained to bring back shot birds.

clue.text: Herein possibly a river (not English)

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of herein may be arranged another way
not with English means the English abbreviation is dropped from the pool

explanation.surface: Somewhere in here, maybe, is a foreign river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges HEREIN and 'not' drops one E from it, leaving HRIN E: five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The major waterway of western Europe, flowing from Switzerland to the North Sea.

clue.text: Motorway up: the drill left to force some action?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the motorway is read from the bottom

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI
PE, physical education, is school drill

explanation.surface: Roadworks on the motorway force the drivers into action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses MI to IM. The M1 is Britain's first long motorway, London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive or urge someone forward into doing something.

clue.text: Provisional shelter — one at centre of St Ives

parts.note: a tent is a canvas shelter
a means one

indicators.note: the centre of the words means all but their first and last letters

explanation.surface: A temporary campsite sits in the middle of a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes TIVE from 'St Ives'; 'at' is a link. St Ives is a Cornish seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Tentative plans are provisional, not yet settled.

clue.text: Propose for election to lodge

definitions.meaning: to house a guest for the night

explanation.definitionFit: Nominate a candidate; also give someone accommodation.

clue.text: "Time off" all wrapped up?

parts.note: a break from work bundled together in one arranged deal, as if gift-wrapped

explanation.definitionFit: A trip with travel and lodging sold together as one deal.

clue.text: See 27
